title: Derived GAGA comparison for finite locally free coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective scheme over $\mathbf C$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism], with analytification $M$ and ringed-space morphism $\pi$ as in [lem-sfb-smooth-analytification-cotangent]. Let $F$ be any finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], with no constant-rank assumption. Put $F^{\mathrm{an}}=\mathcal O_M\otimes_{\pi^{-1}\mathcal O_X}\pi^{-1}F$ and let $a_F:F\to\pi_*F^{\mathrm{an}}$ send $s$ to $1\otimes s$. All derived functors in the following formula are taken on sheaves of $\mathbf C$-vector spaces, and $F[0]$ denotes the complex with $F$ in degree zero [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The canonical morphism induced by $F[0]\to R\pi_*(F^{\mathrm{an}}[0])$ and composition of derived global sections is an isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf C})$:
$$g_F:R\Gamma(X,F[0])\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma(M,F^{\mathrm{an}}[0]).$$
Here $D^+$ consists of derived objects with cohomology zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. The arrow is the canonical one induced by $a_F$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. The assertion includes the empty scheme and finitely many components of different dimensions.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, Géométrie algébrique et géométrie analytique, §11 (canonical comparison), §12 Theorem 1, printed pp.18--22, https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1956__6__1_0.pdf. Derived reformulation of Theorem 1 restricted to finite locally free coefficients, using the canonical map of §11; no naturality for non-O-linear operators is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf C}$ from the definition of projectivity. The projective-field coordinate theorem, for $i$ and for $\mathrm{id}_P$, makes $X,P$ Noetherian and proper with coherent structure sheaves. Properness includes separatedness and finite type. A finite locally free $F$ is locally a finite free module, hence quasi-coherent of finite type, so the locally Noetherian coherence criterion applies. Thus $G=i_*F$ is coherent by the closed-immersion theorem. On each standard chart of $P$, degree-zero localization is $\mathbf C[z_l/z_j:l\ne j]$: degree-zero monomials are products of these ratios, with no polynomial relations. These charts are affine $n$-spaces. Affine-space smoothness and locality on the source prove that $P$ is smooth. The analytification theorem now applies to both $X$ and $P$, including their closed embedding.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: For any separated smooth finite-type complex scheme $T$ used below and any module $E$, define $\epsilon^q_{T,E}=H^q(g_E)$, using the same canonical arrow as in the statement. All sites of opens are sets in a common enlarged universe. Module sheaves over either the structure ring or the constant ring $\mathbf C$ have enough injectives. Derived evaluation on the terminal open identifies their cohomology with underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology, naturally and identically in degree zero; scalar multiplication gives the same $\mathbf C$-action. The single-object derived-functor identification computes $H^q(R\Gamma(E[0]))$ by an injective resolution for $q\ge0$. Choose injective $\mathbf C$-sheaf resolutions $E\to I$ and $E^{\mathrm{an}}\to J$. Exact inverse image makes $\pi^{-1}E[0]\to\pi^{-1}I$ a degreewise monic quasi-isomorphism. The injective lifting lemma extends $\pi^{-1}E\to E^{\mathrm{an}}\to J$ to $\pi^{-1}I\to J$, adjoint to $u:I\to\pi_*J$. The acyclic-resolution normalization identifies $\Gamma(u)$ with the canonical derived-sections arrow, after forgetting to abelian sheaves. Indeed injective module terms are abelian-global-acyclic by derived evaluation. Consequently $\epsilon^0$ sends $s$ to $1\otimes s$ and $\epsilon^q$ is the underlying inverse-image cohomology map followed by the coefficient map.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: The inverse-image cohomology maps commute with connecting homomorphisms by the topos pullback delta theorem. For $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$, analytic pullback exactness makes the analytified row short exact, and the natural coefficient maps give a morphism from the inverse-image row to this row. The morphism-of-sequences clause of the same delta theorem then proves that the maps $\epsilon^q$ commute with its connecting homomorphisms. Long exact sequences exist by the derived-functor theorem: sections preserve kernels and finite sums because both are computed sectionwise; this verifies left exactness and additivity on either topological space. Thus every algebraic short exact sequence gives a commutative comparison of long exact cohomology sequences, with the actual maps $H^q(g_E)$ of Step 2.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: Closed direct image does not change cohomology on either underlying topological space, by the closed-embedding cohomology theorem; use derived evaluation to identify module, $\mathbf C$-sheaf and abelian cohomology as in Step 2. The analytic closed-direct-image isomorphism gives $(i_*F)^{\mathrm{an}}=i^{\mathrm{an}}_*F^{\mathrm{an}}$ and identifies its coefficient map with $i_*a_F$. Therefore the comparison for $i_*F$ identifies with the comparison for $F$. This is a commutative square for the canonical maps: on resolutions it is the direct-image identification of sections, and the augmentation sends each section to $1\otimes s$ on both routes. The same observation applies to any closed embedding of smooth schemes encountered below, in particular a coordinate hyperplane.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: Record the elementary exact-sequence argument used repeatedly below. In a commutative diagram of five-term exact sequences of vector spaces, if the four outside vertical maps are isomorphisms then the middle map is an isomorphism. For injectivity, a middle element mapping to zero comes from the preceding term; its lower preimage comes from the first term, so lift from the first term and subtract to obtain zero in the preceding term. For surjectivity, map a lower middle element to the next term and lift there; its next image is zero by injectivity at the last term, so exactness supplies an upper middle preimage. Their difference comes from the lower preceding term; lift there and adjust. Apply this to the appropriate five consecutive terms of Step 3, inserting zero groups in negative degrees. Hence if comparisons for any two members of a short exact sequence are isomorphisms in every degree, so are those for the third.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: For every $n\ge0$, the comparison for $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n}$ is an isomorphism in every degree. The algebraic twist-cohomology calculation gives constants $\mathbf C$ in degree zero and zero in higher degree, including $n=0$. The analytic structure-sheaf theorem gives unique constant global functions and vanishing in positive degree, in the category of $\mathbf C$-sheaves. Under $(\mathcal O_P)^{\mathrm{an}}=\mathcal O_{P^{\mathrm{an}}}$, the canonical degree-zero comparison is the identity on constants. The higher-degree comparisons are maps between zero groups. For $n=0$, every twist has its single standard-chart frame and is $\mathcal O_P$; its analytic frame identifies the coefficient map with the same constants map. This proves the all-twists induction base.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text:
Induct on $n$ to prove the comparison for every twist $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n}(d)$, $d\in\mathbf Z$. For $n\ge1$ use the fixed coordinate hyperplane $j:H=V(z_n)\hookrightarrow P$, so $H=\mathbf P^{n-1}$ and $j^*\mathcal O_P(d)=\mathcal O_H(d)$ by the displayed standard-chart transition functions. Its structure sheaf is coherent by the projective-field coordinate theorem. On a chart $z_j\ne0$, multiplication by the section $z_n$ is multiplication by $z_n/z_j$ (or $1$ if $j=n$). It is injective on the polynomial coordinate ring and its localizations, since a nonzero polynomial has nonzero product with $z_n/z_j$. Local frames give injectivity on every twist. Apply the fixed-hyperplane sequence with $E=\mathcal O_P$:
$$0\to\mathcal O_P(d-1)\to\mathcal O_P(d)\to j_*\mathcal O_H(d)\to0.$$
The induction hypothesis on $H$ and Step 4 make the third comparison an isomorphism for every $d$. Steps 3 and 5 show that comparison for $d$ is an isomorphism in all degrees if and only if comparison for $d-1$ is. Step 6 supplies $d=0$; induction in both directions on the integers proves every $d$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: The comparison also holds for a finite direct sum of twists. If $E=\bigoplus_r\mathcal O_P(d_r)$, its finite biproduct injections and projections satisfy $p_r i_s=\delta_{rs}$ and $\sum_r i_r p_r=1$. Tensor pullback and cohomology preserve these identities, since they are additive. Naturality of the coefficient maps identifies $\epsilon^q_E$ with the block diagonal map whose blocks are the twist comparisons of Step 7; the block diagonal sum of their inverses is its inverse. Empty sums give the zero sheaf.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: Apply the finite twist-resolution theorem over $k=\mathbf C$ to the coherent $G=i_*F$ on $P$. Write its finite exact resolution as $0\to E_\ell\to\cdots\to E_0\to G\to0$, with each $E_j$ a finite sum of twists. If $\ell=0$ the augmentation is already an isomorphism. Otherwise put $K_0=G$ and $K_{j+1}=\ker(E_j\to K_j)$ for $0\le j<\ell$; exactness identifies $K_\ell$ with $E_\ell$ and gives $0\to K_{j+1}\to E_j\to K_j\to0$. Analytic exactness applies to these module sheaves, without any extra coherence hypothesis on the kernels. Step 8 proves comparison for $K_\ell$ and each $E_j$. Descending induction on $j$, using Steps 3 and 5 for each displayed short exact sequence, proves comparison for $K_0=G$ in every nonnegative degree. Step 4 transfers this to $F$ on $X$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Serre, GAGA, §§11--13, printed pp.18--22; agent-written derived reformulation and finite-resolution variant.

proof.text: We have proved that $H^q(g_F)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$ for the specified canonical arrow. Both derived section objects have zero negative cohomology, since they are computed by nonnegative injective resolutions of sheaves placed in degree zero. Thus $H^q(g_F)$ is an isomorphism for every integer $q$. The bounded-below derived-category cohomology criterion proves that $g_F$ itself is an isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathbf C})$. No rank, connectedness or equidimensionality was used: a projective embedding and coherent finite resolution work for all components at once. If $X$ is empty or $F=0$, both derived section complexes are zero and the same canonical map is their unique isomorphism.

The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live, where the item is unsplit and no other group has split it. The canonical arrow is the one treated: Step 2's acyclic-resolution node gives res_f(a_F), which is exactly g_F, and the forgetful functor from C-vector spaces to abelian groups is exact and faithful. Step 3 uses pullback-delta with its clause on morphisms of short exact sequences, plus analytic exactness. Step 4 handles closed direct image through i_* of acyclic resolutions and the coefficient identification a_{i_*F}=i_*a_F. Steps 6-7: the base case H^*(P^n,O) matches on both sides and the hyperplane ladder covers d to d-1 in both directions; I checked every hypothesis of fixed-hyperplane-restriction (s=z_n, O_H coherent, injectivity on charts). Step 9 resolves G by finite sums of twists (Stacks 00OQ/01YS/03GM read at their labels), and analytic exactness needs no coherence of the kernels. Step 10 applies the D^+ isomorphism criterion. All 4 new nodes are true (Serre GAGA Prop.10, Prop.11, §13 Lemma 4; graded syzygy with length at most n+1), statement-only, self-contained and not duplicates (the P^1 resolution node covers only P^1). Edge cases checked: X empty, F=0, n=0, mixed component dimensions, negative twists, length 0. Batch 5: the euler-polynomial closure reaches only a generic forward-difference polynomial lemma, and the other two closures reach general definitions (geometric morphism, tensor-pullback comparison); none is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality. The 12 declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA citation. Serre GAGA is not on disk, is listed as WANTED, and the proof is correctly marked by agent.
